title: Search Insert Position
description:
Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a target value `target`, return the 0-based index if the target is found. If not, return the index where it would be if it were inserted in order.

You must write an algorithm with `O(log n)` runtime complexity.
constraints: nums contains distinct values sorted in ascending order.
hints: This problem asks for the lower bound: the smallest index i such that nums[i] >= target (or nums.length if all elements are smaller).
Use binary search over the half-open range [0, nums.length] so that left converges directly to the insertion index.

examples.explanation: 2 is not in nums; inserting it between 1 and 3 places it at index 1.
7 is greater than all elements in nums, so it belongs at index 4.
